A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe DyG-Mamba. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive rewriting, reorganization, and some internal inconsistencies.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original link-prediction and node-classification results, ablations, robustness tests, and computational-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original benchmark results, including additional large-graph evaluation, timespan-function ablations, convergence measurements, and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: V1 Equation 5's cosine/linear/SiLU timespan mapping is replaced by a positive, monotone exponential function in v2 Equation 11. V2 adds spectral-norm constraints to the B/C projection weights. Its link-prediction equations and Algorithm 2 omit v1's linear cross-attention stage, although Table 9 inconsistently still lists one cross-attention layer.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on tgbl-coin-v2, containing 638K nodes and 22.8M temporal edges, beyond the retained twelve benchmarks. Link prediction and node classification remain the evaluated tasks; the latter's results move to Appendix D.

E2.justification: The nine principal baselines and appendix FreeDyG comparisons remain. V2 adds an explicit DyGFormer-without-co-occurrence comparator in Table 12 and a direct Vanilla Mamba convergence comparison in Table 7. The large-graph experiment uses existing baseline methods.

E3.justification: The original split ratios, AP/AUC metrics, negative-sampling strategies, and nominal 100-epoch budget remain. New evaluations extend sequence length to 4096 and measure convergence at 20-epoch intervals. Appendix D.2 specifies relaxed transductive evaluation allowing unseen nodes, qualifying v1's seen-node description; this does not establish that the earlier DyGLib experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds alternative timespan-function and normalization tests, convergence analysis, co-occurrence and skip-connection ablations, and sensitivity to block count, state dimension, and expansion factor. It removes v1's preliminary time/position-encoding comparison and cross-attention ablations. Several existing time-information ablations are retained or renamed, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The stated repetition count changes from five runs in v1 to ten runs with different random seeds in v2, which explicitly specifies mean and standard deviation. Uncertainty values already appeared in v1. Student's t-test p-values disappear with the removal of v1 Figure 1.

E6.justification: Many link-prediction entries are replaced alongside the method and reported run-count revisions. For example, random-negative inductive AP changes from 90.05 to 96.64 on Can. Parl. and from 59.52 to 55.25 on US Legis. (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 3). New scalability and analysis results appear, while node-classification results remain unchanged in v2 Table 11.

T1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the diagonal-state update theorem and proof, while retaining much of the causal-attention expansion. It adds Theorem 4.3 and Appendix E.3's spectral-norm-based output-perturbation bound. V1's standalone ZOH theorem/proof and linear-attention derivation are no longer presented separately.

C1.justification: Linear cross-attention is removed from the headline contributions. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion instead emphasize timespan-informed forgetting and review-cycle-inspired noise control with spectral constraints. Claims of efficient long-sequence modeling and state-of-the-art performance on most datasets remain.

C2.justification: V2 substantially develops the forgetting/review interpretation and attributes robustness to Lipschitz-stable input-dependent projections. It adds explanations involving boundedness, saturation, and instability for alternative timespan functions, while removing cross-attention-based explanations of gains. The limitations concerning interaction types, scalability, and transfer to other domains are largely retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds DyG-Mamba code-access links, explicit zero-vector handling for missing features, and clarification of the relaxed transductive implementation and CAWN adaptation. Hardware, software, and most configuration tables remain. The earlier early-stopping patience of 20 and detailed baseline implementation descriptions are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 substantially revises positioning by discussing DG-Mamba, GraphSSM, and PIVEM, distinguishing discrete-time graph SSMs from its continuous-time setting and interpreting PIVEM as a restricted SSM case. V1's extended comparisons with vanilla Mamba, DyGFormer, and TCL are removed or condensed, alongside substantial citation changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Quantitative/qualitative evaluation is reorganized into setup, effectiveness, efficiency, training, robustness, and case-study sections. Appendices are reordered and consolidated, and lengthy related-work and dataset descriptions are removed.

P2.justification: The ACM two-column presentation becomes a NeurIPS single-column layout. The architecture diagram is redrawn, diagnostic and ablation figures are removed, and new scalability, convergence, and sensitivity displays appear. Existing tables and plots are reordered, resized, or relocated, including node classification moving to the appendix.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical coverage through large-graph evaluation and targeted analyses, and adds code-access information. However, its new robustness proof assumes bounds on generated B/C parameters that do not follow from the stated weight constraints, then uses a sum-to-integral approximation as a bound. Cross-attention specifications conflict internally, and Tables 3 and 16 inconsistently attribute TCL/GraphMixer results. These benefits and new reliability problems prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
